cost-of-living.name: Rising costs
cost-of-living.line: Everything costs more each year, and my pay hasn't kept up.
cost-of-living.why: Says what inflation feels like in a day, keeps the pay gap from the alias, and the name matches what the ID names.

cost-of-living.name: Inflation
cost-of-living.line: I can't keep up as prices rise faster than my pay.
cost-of-living.why: Keeps the familiar name and adds the pay side, which is what makes rising prices hurt.

it-all-goes-up.name: Inequality
it-all-goes-up.line: I see the gap between people with plenty and people who are struggling keep growing.
it-all-goes-up.why: Same meaning, fixes the awkward "those struggling grow" so the sentence reads naturally out loud.

it-all-goes-up.name: Growing gap
it-all-goes-up.line: I see the people who own things get more while everyone else falls behind.
it-all-goes-up.why: Brings back the earlier wording people recognized, in plainer words than "inequality".

ai-and-jobs.name: AI job losses
ai-and-jobs.line: I worry AI will replace people's jobs and no one has a plan for them.
ai-and-jobs.why: Names the problem rather than the technology, matching the ID, and says what "no one's ready" means.

ai-and-jobs.name: AI and jobs
ai-and-jobs.line: I worry AI will take people's work and no one's ready for it.
ai-and-jobs.why: A light touch: the name says what about AI worries people, and the line keeps its voice.

no-floor.name: No safety net
no-floor.line: If I lose my job or get sick, I know there's nothing to fall back on.
no-floor.why: Says what falling means in a day instead of a metaphor, and the name states the problem so it matches the heading's other problem names.

childcare-costs.name: Childcare costs
childcare-costs.line: I can't afford childcare, even though I need it to work.
childcare-costs.why: The name says the problem is the cost, and the line adds the bind most parents describe.

rent-eats-everything.name: High rent
rent-eats-everything.line: Rent takes so much of my pay that little is left for anything else.
rent-eats-everything.why: Brings back the ID's "rent eats everything" in plain words, and the name states the problem.

cant-afford-kids.name: Can't afford kids
cant-afford-kids.line: I want kids but can't afford to raise them.
cant-afford-kids.why: The earlier name says the problem plainly, where "Starting a family" reads like a topic, and it matches the ID.
